display.title: Episode 150: Dama ben Nesina's Diamond, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: The first Mitzvah Time phone winner, two ways to honor parents, a four-year-old guest from Madrid leads the Shema, and Dama ben Nesina refuses a fortune rather than wake his father.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens by describing the homemade instruments listeners use for the Hakochainik march, and everyone marches along. After the sponsor's cheese commercial comes Mitzvah Time: Uncle Yossi telephones a listener, who correctly answers that the reward for honoring parents is long life and wins the first prize of the new contest. This week's mitzvos are never to sit in a parent's own chair, and never to interrupt a parent who is speaking. A four-year-old visitor from Madrid, Spain, leads the Shema. The story from the Gemara concludes: Dama ben Nesina will not wake his sleeping father to fetch the key to the diamond, even when the Kohen Gadol's messengers raise their offer, and they leave without it. The next year a perfectly red heifer, a parah adumah, is born on his farm, and the same messengers pay him what they had offered for the stone. Uncle Yossi points out that if a non-Jew was rewarded like this, our reward for this commanded mitzvah is even greater. The show ends with a letter and riddle from the mailbox, an invitation to send essays on kibbud av va'em, and the winners of the Shofar Gadol drawing contest.
display.lesson: Honor your parents even when it costs you; Hashem sees and repays it many times over.
